expectations.note: A row-per-line table carries order, multiplicity, presence, unit and grain, and every claim has evidence.
A tree drops the ordering and merges line occurrences into nodes; the projection still renders something.
A chart keeps the series but not the row occurrence identity; a point is not a line.
A boolean form collapses the five presence states and drops the ordered occurrence.
An order-grain panel over line rows declares an inverse; the aggregate row has no unique line to write back to.
The multigraph cannot become a tree without losing parallel edges and extra parents, so it is lossy rather than preserved.
The source carries domain and observation; the Gantt declares only domain, and the axes are a different pair, so the report is refused rather than called lossy.
Domain and observation time reported as playback time; the window tail is unread; and the sample order is generated by the audio device rather than carried from the source.
JPY to USD without a policy or an instant is unqualified, not a silent default.
The chart aggregates invoices into a tenant-month series; the value survives and the per-invoice identity does not.
A point rendered as a delta shares the unit string but not the arithmetic contract; the form is refused.
